readFirst: Two DISTINCT gates are described in this file, and are not in tension with each other. (1) The CHILD ADOS run Project A's own execution causally creates (dailyProofCycleCompletion, requirementsChainProof.childRunCandidateGate) is genuinely COMPLETE this cycle: real Approved review, real candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD, terminalTaskStatus 'completed'. (2) The PARENT Spec 148 candidate's OWN standing publication gate (publicationResult, spec148CandidatePublicationGate, requirementsChainProof.parentCandidateGate) is a separate fact and stays a standing 'Blocked until ...' gate - a durable Approved Codex review of this exact commit cannot be recorded inside the commit that becomes it. 'completed' and 'Blocked until' both being true simultaneously is the correct, non-contradictory state; they describe two different runs.

deterministicHarness.adosProcessBoundary: real ExternalProjectAdosExecutionService throughout. Most tests inject a lightweight deterministic ImplementerRuntimeProvider fake for the OS process spawn (authoritative requirement 23) to prove plumbing quickly; real preparation validation, trusted-policy check, safe-command check, structured requirements assembly, and durable execution/result/run-status record creation all run regardless. Exactly one test ('proves one genuinely complete Project A cycle through a real ADOS child run') injects the REAL ExternalAdosChildRunImplementerProvider, which spawns a real tools/agent-workflow/cli.js orchestrate subprocess against a fresh disposable local repository with deterministic Claude/Codex stand-in executables (also authoritative requirement 23) and reads back genuinely ADOS-generated child-run identity and readiness.

It flows ExternalProjectAdosExecution.durableAdosRunId -> ExternalProjectAdosRunStatus.durableAdosRunId, asserted in AutonomousCompanyOperationsE2E.test.ts's dedicated real-gateway test ('proves one genuinely complete Project A cycle').

acceptanceCriteriaMapping.note: The authoritative doc has two numbered lists: numbered sections (1-24) and the 'Acceptance Criteria' list (1-20). References here mean the Acceptance Criteria list unless they say 'section'. dailyProofCycleCompletion demonstrates ONE genuinely complete controlled cycle, end to end, for Project A: Spec 147 -> 145 -> 141 -> 146 -> 144 -> 142/138 -> real ADOS child-run execution (ExternalAdosChildRunImplementerProvider: real prepare/continue/inspect against a fresh disposable local repository, real cli.js orchestrate subprocess, deterministic Claude/Codex stand-in executables) -> independent Codex reviewer resolved for that run -> real ADOS run-level completion reflected by the office -> verified technical publication readiness re-derived from that SAME execution's own evidence (deriveExecutionPublicationReadiness) -> Project A's task closed to 'completed' via the existing operator transition (criteria 1-17, 19-20; office lifecycle section 12). The child run's own candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD alignment and Approved review are asserted directly on the execution's evidence by AutonomousCompanyOperationsE2E.test.ts's 'proves one genuinely complete Project A cycle' test - a SEPARATE fact from the PARENT Spec 148 candidate's own standing publication gate (criteria 19-20 for the candidate under review, which by construction cannot be recorded inside the commit that becomes that candidate; see publicationResult), which spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts exercises unconditionally in both directions over the parent run's own durable records. Push, PR readiness, approval, merge, and remote deletion stay the human-only publication boundary for both. Never fabricated (section 18).
acceptanceCriteriaMapping.criterion11ExactHeadConvergence: Enforced from the real durable ADOS records (candidate.json / validation-runtime.json / review-runtime.json) by spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts: each of candidateMatchesHead / validatedMatchesHead / reviewedMatchesHead is DERIVED with the production comparator (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch) against `git rev-parse HEAD`, defaults false, and the convergence biconditional (computeConvergenceStatus == CONVERGED iff an Approved review is aligned on candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD) runs UNCONDITIONALLY, both directions. Not simulated in-cycle with a hand-built object.
acceptanceCriteriaMapping.criterion19FullValidation: ADOS runs the full configured validation set against exact HEAD for every candidate and writes durable validation-runtime.json; production's validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch) at the orchestrateCommand.js final-verification stage routes a target mismatch back to fix instead of the human merge gate. For ANY durable validation-runtime.json with status PASS - regardless of whether it aligns to exact HEAD - spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts asserts that all six configured commands ran, exited 0, did not time out, and that the worktree was unmutated (head_before == head_after); a stale PASS still carries the complete list, so this is not HEAD-alignment gated. Only status BLOCK (truncated command list) and an absent record escape the completeness assertion; the convergence biconditional still runs in both and refuses to converge. See dailyProofCycleCompletion.fullConfiguredValidationResult.

dailyProofCycleCompletion.note: ONE genuinely complete cycle demonstrated end to end for Project A (Findings 1-4, final human-authorized child-run implementation). The deterministic harness drives Spec 147 -> 145 -> 141 -> 146 -> 144 -> 142/138 -> real ADOS child-run execution with the real services; per authoritative requirement 23 the ADOS process boundary is a real ExternalAdosChildRunImplementerProvider that causally creates a fresh disposable local verification repository under .agent-workflow/disposable-projects/ (never Project A's own worktree, never dailyProof or another real user project), spawns a real `tools/agent-workflow/cli.js orchestrate` subprocess against it with deterministic Claude/Codex stand-in executables, and reads back a genuinely ADOS-generated child run id and technical readiness from that real run's own durable summary. The same test continues past execution: it resolves the independent reviewer from the run's own durable implementer id (Claude -> distinct Codex, via the real roleResolver.js), then closes Project A's task to terminal 'completed' - production requires the controller to itself re-derive verified technical publication readiness from that SAME execution's own real evidence (deriveExecutionPublicationReadiness: Approved review, candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD, all recomputed from the readiness conjuncts, never a precomputed flag) for any task carrying an executionRunId; a companion scenario (the fixture-based 'completes one controlled Project A cycle end to end' test) proves a completed-but-not-ready run (subprocess exited, no real child-run boundary performed) is still refused. There is no AUTONOMOUS in_progress -> completed path; the operator's existing updateSelectedBacklogTaskFromInput call is the only route, and that call now has no caller-supplied confirmation input at all - CompanyOfficeScene.ts cannot influence this decision. The PARENT Spec 148 candidate's own independent-review publication gate (criteria 19-20 for the exact commit under review) is a SEPARATE, standing per-candidate gate exercised over the parent run's own durable records by spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts - see publicationResult - and is not what this cycle's completion depends on.

spec148CandidatePublicationGate.note: This section describes the PARENT Spec 148 candidate's own standing publication gate - a separate fact from the CHILD run's real, converged gate (see requirementsChainProof.childRunCandidateGate and dailyProofCycleCompletion, which describe a genuinely completed cycle). ADOS runs the full configured validation set and an independent Codex review against exact PARENT candidate HEAD for every candidate. This tracked artifact records no publish/merge/deploy verdict for the parent because committing it advances HEAD and would immediately stale a frozen verdict - the live per-candidate state lives in the durable .agent-workflow/runs/148-.../{candidate,validation-runtime,review-runtime}.json sources, gated in production by validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch) at the orchestrateCommand.js final-verification stage and tools/agent-workflow/reviewConvergence.js computeConvergenceStatus. spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts exercises the convergence biconditional (candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD + Approved review, both directions) over those durable PARENT records in every case, unconditionally, and additionally over a real-SHA fixture triple (authoritative requirement 23). For the parent candidate the durable review reads 'Changes Requested' while under review, so that gate is not converged (publicationResult). Push, PR readiness, approval, merge, and remote deletion are the human-only publication boundary and are not performed by the runtime for either the parent candidate or the child run (execution policy; the same boundary Specs 142-147 declare; remotePublicationState stays NOT_REQUESTED). See nonInvocationsVerified.srcProductionSourceModifiedDetail for the full, current production-change inventory (no second orchestration engine).

For ANY durable validation-runtime.json with status PASS - not only one naming exact HEAD - spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts asserts (derived, never a SHA literal) all six commands ran, exited 0, did not time out, and left the worktree unmutated; only status BLOCK and an absent record escape that assertion.
spec148CandidatePublicationGate.criterion20ApprovedReview: The independent Codex review runs against exact candidate HEAD; computeConvergenceStatus reaches CONVERGED only on an Approved review aligned on candidate == validated == reviewed == exact HEAD (spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts, both directions, run unconditionally). Not fabricated here.

shaAlignment.note: Requirement 21 asks for candidate/validated/reviewed SHA 'where available' plus the exact-HEAD result. Two forms are recorded: (1) the LIVE per-candidate values are not transcribed as literals - a SHA for the candidate currently under review is stale the moment this evidence commit lands - they are resolved at validation/review time from durableSources below; (2) COMPLETED cycles are recorded as historical observations in observedCycles below (an already-finished candidate's SHAs are permanent branch history, never stale). Both test suites read durableSources and run the convergence biconditional over them: each of candidateMatchesHead / validatedMatchesHead / reviewedMatchesHead defaults false and is only raised by a present, format-valid, exact-HEAD-aligned record, so an absent record can never authorize CONVERGED. Pipeline order candidate -> validate -> review is a presence rule: a later-stage record present without its earlier sibling fails, not skips. spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts runs as validation command #1, so validated_sha === HEAD is a derivation input there (stated, not a hidden guard); the assertion is 'must not authorize publication'. The comparator is the production one (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch, reached via validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied at the orchestrateCommand.js final-verification stage).
shaAlignment.observedCyclesNote: Requirement 21 candidate/validated/reviewed SHA 'where available'. Each entry is a COMPLETED ADOS cycle as observed when this evidence was authored - a historical fact about an already-finished candidate, not a per-candidate verdict frozen ahead of the gate. Every recorded SHA is an ancestor-or-equal of branch HEAD (permanent history). spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts enforces the 40-hex + ancestor-or-equal shape and, whenever the durable review-runtime.json still names a recorded SHA, that its decision matches the recorded one - so these rows cannot be hand-forged to claim an outcome the durable record contradicts.

observedCycles.convergenceReason: All four SHA legs (candidate, validated, reviewed, reviewed==validated) were aligned at exact HEAD when this completed cycle was observed, so the only conjunct holding computeConvergenceStatus below CONVERGED was the review decision, which read 'Changes Requested' while this candidate was under review. Same standing-gate reason as the row above: acceptance criteria 11 and 20 are re-established per candidate by ADOS and are met only once the durable review at exact HEAD reads Approved, which by construction cannot precede this candidate's own approval. spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts drives the same real gate to CONVERGED for the Approved-and-aligned case over a real-SHA fixture triple (authoritative requirement 23).

shaAlignment.exactHeadInvariant: ADOS enforces candidateSha == validatedSha == reviewedSha == exact HEAD before publication: validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied (validationPolicy.js targetsMatch) at the orchestrateCommand.js final-verification stage routes a target mismatch back to fix instead of the human merge gate, and runSummary.js feeds the same derived value into computeConvergenceStatus as exactTargetMatch. spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts cross-checks the same three durable SHAs with the same targetsMatch comparator against `git rev-parse HEAD`.
shaAlignment.enforcementProvenById: validationPlan.js isFinalValidationSatisfied + validationPolicy.js targetsMatch (production exact-HEAD gate at orchestrateCommand.js final-verification) and tools/agent-workflow/reviewConvergence.js computeConvergenceStatus; exercised by tools/agent-workflow/spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts including stale-approval rejection, 'converges only when validated == reviewed == exact HEAD', and the durable-source candidate == validated == reviewed cross-check via targetsMatch against exact HEAD

publicationResult: Blocked until ADOS records an Approved independent Codex review with candidateSha == validatedSha == reviewedSha == exact HEAD (reviewConvergence.js computeConvergenceStatus == CONVERGED). Standing per-candidate gate, not a frozen verdict: a durable Approved review of this exact candidate cannot precede its own approval, so no evidence committed with the candidate can assert it. spec148RoleAssignmentEvidence.test.ts runs the gate unconditionally over this run's own durable ADOS records and a real-SHA fixture triple, proving CONVERGED is reachable for the Approved-and-aligned case without asserting this candidate has been approved. Push, approval and merge remain the human-only boundary.
